question: What is the probability that a random chord of a circle is longer than the side of the inscribed equilateral triangle?
finding: With 100,000 chords per method, 33.1% are long when the endpoints are random, 50.1% when a point on a random radius is and 25.2% when the midpoint is, and only the random-radius method keeps its answer when the question is put to a smaller circle.
limit: The simulation shows that each procedure has its own answer; it cannot say which procedure "at random" means, because the question does not.
